question.problem:
Let $V=C[0,1],$ the vector space of functions that are continuous over $[0,1].$ Given that the inner product on $V$ is defined as 

$$
⟨x(t),y(t)⟩={\int }_{0}^{1}x(t)y(t)\,\text{d}t,
$$

find the distance between $f(t)=3t$ and $g(t)=-3t+3$ with respect to the inner product.
question.worked_solution:
The distance between $f(t)=3t$ and $g(t)=-3t+3$ with respect to the given inner product is

$$
\begin{aligned}d & =‖f(t)-g(t)‖ \\  & =‖3t-(-3t+3)‖ \\  & =‖6t-3‖ \\  & =\sqrt{⟨6t-3,6t-3⟩}.\end{aligned}
$$

Computing the inner product, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨6t-3,6t-3⟩ & ={\int }_{0}^{1}(6t-3)^{2}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}(36{t}^{2}-36t+9)\text{d}t \\  & =[12{t}^{3}-18{t}^{2}+9t]_{0}^{1} \\  & =(12-18+9)-0 \\  & =3.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the distance is $d=\sqrt{3}.$
